title: CVE-2026-102764: BeyondTrust Zero-Day Exploited
content_md: BeyondTrust has disclosed CVE-2026-102764 , a critical Remote Support vulnerability exploited as a zero-day weeks before customers received a patch. The attack began on August 29, 2026 , when one BeyondTrust-hosted Remote Support instance and one self-hosted appliance were compromised. BeyondTrust detected the hosted incident during proactive hunting on September 28, reproduced the entry vector that day, released patches on October 8, and publicly disclosed the CVE on October 15. Researchers attribute the activity to ARMORY CASTLE , formerly tracked as UNC5221, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor known for targeting edge appliances. What Is CVE-2026-102764? CVE-2026-102764 is an improper origin validation vulnerability (CWE-290) in an internal Remote Support messaging component. According to BeyondTrust, the component did not adequately validate where received messages originated. Under the right conditions, this allows remote attackers to trigger file operations without authentication or user interaction. BeyondTrust rates the flaw Critical with a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.3 .
